question: Do two CMP 170HX cards in one box beat one, and is TP=2 worth it without NVLink or P2P?

hardware.topology: PHB (both cards traverse the PCIe host bridge; no NVLink, no PCIe switch)

interconnect.gns_meaning: GPU not supported - P2P is fused off in the CMP SKU itself
interconnect.note: P2P is NOT blocked by IOMMU or ACS; it is unavailable on the mining SKU. No BIOS or kernel change recovers it.
interconnect.d2d_vs_h2d: Inter-GPU copies are host-staged, so device-to-device is no faster than host-to-device.
interconnect.vllm_warning: Custom allreduce is disabled because your platform lacks GPU P2P capability or P2P test failed.

software.note: Identical engine and flags to results/lab-2026-08-21.json, so TP=1 here is directly comparable to the single-card lab.

tp1.power_note: Box total across both cards; the idle second card contributes ~40 W.

two_tp1_servers.layout: Two independent vLLM servers, CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 on port 8000 and =1 on port 8001, TP=1 each, no collectives between them.
two_tp1_servers.note: At 16 agents this beats TP=2 by 1.8x (754 vs 415). At 32 agents, which TP=2 cannot serve at max-num-seqs 16, it reaches 1253 tok/s - 3.0x the TP=2 16-agent figure on the same two cards.
two_tp1_servers.tradeoff: Each server is limited to a 64 GB card and a 1.19M-token KV pool, and you need a load balancer in front. There is no shared KV cache between the two.

capacity_test_72b_tp2.why: The 'use TP=2 when the model does not fit in 64 GB' claim was asserted but never measured. A 72B AWQ checkpoint (39 GiB of weights) is the case that only two cards can serve comfortably.
capacity_test_72b_tp2.context_finding: The 128K attempt was rejected by vLLM: this checkpoint's config.json declares max_position_embeddings=32768. The 128K figure quoted for Qwen2.5-72B requires YaRN rope-scaling, which is off by default. So the 32K ceiling seen on one card was the MODEL's native limit, not a VRAM limit - two cards do not unlock a longer window here without explicitly enabling YaRN.
notes: 72B at TP=2 decodes 37.1 tok/s single-stream - about half the 70.9 tok/s that 27B reaches at TP=2, which tracks the ~2.7x parameter increase against the doubled memory bandwidth.
Batch throughput tops out at 359.7 tok/s at 32 agents, still below what a SINGLE card does with 27B (608 tok/s at 16 agents). Capacity, not speed, is what the second card buys.

Power is inverted versus intuition: 1 agent draws the highest median (436.9 W) and 32 agents the lowest (303.6 W). Under heavy batch the cards spend more time blocked on the host-staged allreduce than computing, so they clock down.
Prefill of 24K tokens takes 51.0 s, consistent with the TP=2 prefill penalty measured on 27B.
capacity_test_72b_tp2.verdict: The capacity claim holds in the sense that matters: 39 GiB of weights plus a 494,848-token KV pool simply does not fit on one 64 GB card at this batch size. But it costs throughput, and it does NOT extend the context window.

pipeline_parallel_pp2.why: PP=2 was listed as an untested alternative to TP=2. Pipeline parallel splits the model by LAYER instead of by tensor, so the only inter-GPU traffic is one activation handoff at the layer boundary per microbatch, rather than an allreduce inside every layer. On hardware without P2P this should matter enormously.
pipeline_parallel_pp2.model: Qwen3.8-27B-W4A16-AWQ (identical checkpoint to the TP=1 and TP=2 runs)
findings: PP=2 beats TP=2 on throughput by 1.46x at 16 agents (604.7 vs 414.5 tok/s) and keeps scaling to 895.2 tok/s at 32 agents, which TP=2 could not reach.

PP=2 matches single-card TP=1 throughput almost exactly at 16 agents (604.7 vs 608.1 tok/s) while holding 2.3x the KV pool (2.76M vs 1.19M tokens). This is the key result: you get the capacity benefit of two cards without the throughput penalty of tensor parallel.

Prefill is where PP=2 wins outright: 14.8 s on 48K tokens versus 27.1 s for TP=1 and 47.4 s for TP=2. That is 3.2x faster than TP=2 and 1.8x faster than a single card, because pipeline stages overlap on the long prefill and the interconnect carries only layer-boundary activations.

PP=2 gives up the TP=2 single-stream gain: 57.5 tok/s, identical to TP=1 (57.5) and below TP=2 (70.9). Pipeline parallel does not split the per-token weight reads, so one stream sees no bandwidth benefit.
KV pool is slightly smaller than TP=2 (2.76M vs 2.98M tokens) because each stage keeps its own activation buffers, but the difference is only 7%.
pipeline_parallel_pp2.verdict: On hardware without P2P, PP=2 dominates TP=2 for every workload except single-stream latency. It is the correct way to use a second card when the model fits but you want a deeper KV pool: full single-card throughput, 2.3x the context capacity, and the fastest prefill measured in this lab.

muse_glimmer_pp2.why: Muse Glimmer was the fastest model measured on a single card (790 tok/s at 16 agents). PP=2 was the best dual-card mode measured on Qwen 27B. This run combines them.
muse_glimmer_pp2.engine: vLLM 0.26.1rc1.dev1078+gfe76112ff (dev build, own venv). Stock 0.27.1 has no MuseGlimmerForConditionalGeneration in its registry.
findings: 1102.6 tok/s at 32 agents is the highest single-endpoint throughput measured anywhere in this lab, beating the 895.2 tok/s that Qwen 27B reached at PP=2 and the 790 tok/s Muse reached on one card.

KV pool is 5,254,908 tokens for 40.09x concurrency at 128K - roughly double the 2.64M single-card figure, and the deepest pool measured in the lab despite bf16 KV (cc 8.0 cannot use FP8 on this checkpoint).
At 16 agents PP=2 gives 626.4 tok/s versus 790 on a single card. The second card does NOT help at moderate concurrency here; the win only appears at 32 agents where a single card runs out of room.
TTFT is 26.0 ms, the lowest in the lab, because the MoE checkpoint activates few parameters per token.
Single-stream decode is 57.1 tok/s, essentially identical to Qwen 27B at PP=2 (57.5). As with Qwen, pipeline parallel gives no single-stream benefit.

Power at 32 agents (422 W median) is the opposite of the 72B TP=2 behaviour, where heavy batch DROVE power down. PP=2 keeps both cards genuinely busy instead of blocking them on a host-staged allreduce.
muse_glimmer_pp2.verdict: Muse on PP=2 is the throughput champion of the lab at 1102.6 tok/s and holds a 5.25M-token KV pool. But the honest caveat is that a single card already delivers 790 tok/s at 16 agents, so the second card only earns its place above ~16 concurrent agents or when the deeper KV pool is the point.

deltas_tp2_vs_tp1.crossover: TP=2 wins below ~3 concurrent agents and loses above it.

findings: TP=2 raises single-stream decode 23% (57.5 -> 70.9 tok/s) because the weights are split and each card moves half as many bytes per token.
TP=2 collapses batch throughput: 608 -> 415 tok/s at 16 agents, a 32% loss. Per-agent falls 43.0 -> 30.4 tok/s. Reproduced three times within 0.3%.

The cause is P2P: nvidia-smi reports GNS (GPU not supported), so vLLM disables its custom allreduce and every layer's collective is host-staged at 5.85 GB/s. At batch 16 the allreduce payload grows with batch size, so the interconnect dominates.
Prefill is 75% slower under TP=2 (27.1 s -> 47.4 s on 48K tokens) - prefill is compute-and-collective heavy and suffers most from the slow link.
The real prize is the KV pool: 1.19M -> 2.98M tokens (9.11x -> 22.77x concurrency at 128K), because both cards' HBM holds cache.
Two cards at 16 agents (415 tok/s) are beaten by ONE card at 16 agents (608 tok/s) while drawing similar power.

Measured directly: two independent TP=1 servers deliver 754 tok/s at 16 agents and 1253 tok/s at 32 agents, versus 415 tok/s for TP=2. Sharding beats tensor-parallel by 1.8x to 3.0x on the same two cards.

recommendation.use_tp2_when: The model does not fit in 64 GB (measured: 72B AWQ, 39 GiB weights, serves at TP=2 and cannot be served on one card with a useful KV pool), or you need a KV pool deeper than one card can hold, or you are latency-bound on a single stream (+23% decode).
recommendation.tp2_does_not_buy_context: Measured: a second card does not extend the context window. The window is set by the checkpoint's max_position_embeddings, not by VRAM. Qwen2.5-72B-AWQ refused 128K at TP=2 because its config declares 32K; 128K needs YaRN rope-scaling enabled explicitly.
recommendation.use_two_tp1_servers_when: You are throughput-bound and the model fits in one card. Measured 3.0x better (1253 vs 415 tok/s). Costs a load balancer and gives up the shared KV pool.
recommendation.use_pp2_when: Measured best all-round use of a second card on this hardware. The model fits in one card but you want a deeper KV pool: PP=2 gives full single-card throughput (604.7 vs 608.1 tok/s at 16 agents), 2.3x the KV pool, and the fastest prefill in the lab (14.8 s on 48K). Prefer it over TP=2 unless single-stream latency is the goal.
recommendation.never_assume: Do not assume TP=2 scales throughput on a card without P2P/NVLink. Measure both. PP=2 was measured 1.46x faster than TP=2 at 16 agents and 3.2x faster on prefill.

caveats: One 27B dense checkpoint on one rental instance. MoE models and larger checkpoints will shift the crossover point.
No accuracy testing; these are throughput numbers only.
Power is nvidia-smi summed across both cards, not a lab-grade shunt. The idle-card baseline (~40 W) is included in TP=1 box totals.
